subject: Medford Square Redevelopment and Parking Concerns
overview: The Council introduced a new social worker and reviewed monthly service statistics and FY24 budget requests. Members also discussed advocacy for senior center parking during the city's upcoming redevelopment of three Medford Square parking lots.

items.title: Approval of Minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes of the previous meeting held on February 2.

items.title: Director's Report
items.summary: Reported that daily center attendance grew by 4% in February and outlined fiscal year 2024 budget requests totaling over $450,000 across city, state, and federal sources.

items.title: New Staff Introduction
items.summary: Introduced Nikki Gregory as the new part-time social worker, who shared her professional background in clinical social work and animal-assisted therapy.

items.title: MassHealth Redetermination
items.summary: Warned seniors to watch for blue redetermination letters from MassHealth to avoid losing benefits following the end of automatic COVID-era renewals.

items.title: Legislative and Legal Reports
items.summary: Discussed the Governor's proposed budget and extension of hybrid meeting options, while warning of phone scams using AI to mimic relatives' voices.

items.title: Old Business
items.summary: Presented a memorial gold leaf for Medhat Lotfi, noted a vacancy on the board, and announced the return of a monthly blood pressure clinic.

items.title: Medford Square Parking Lot Redevelopment
items.summary: Discussed upcoming public meetings regarding the redevelopment of parking lots A, B, and C, with the Director emphasizing that the center requires at least 40 parking spots daily.

items.title: Announcements
items.summary: Announced the annual St. Patrick's Day luncheon and a $1,000 medical scholarship opportunity offered by Medford Senior Citizens Incorporated.
